source_spans.locator: Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5(4) (1992), published pp.297-300, abstract/introduction and Section 1.1 opening: the proposed representation replaces separable probability-by-probability weighting with a rank-dependent cumulative construction, applies to finite risky and uncertain prospects, and treats gains and losses separately

Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5(4) (1992), published pp.300-301, Section 1.1 formal definition: finite outcomes are arranged in increasing order; state events form a partition; positive and negative parts are separated; two sign-specific capacities generate rank-marginal coefficients from nested cumulative events; overall prospect value is the sum of the two branch values

Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5(4) (1992), published pp.301-302, risky special case and relation to previous work: for additive outcome probabilities, sign-specific probability functions transform cumulative probability sums; the construction applies to any finite prospect and allows different gain-side and loss-side weighting

Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5(4) (1992), published p.303 and pp.316-317, value/weighting shape assumptions and Discussion: the reference point separates gains from losses; valuation uses a two-part cumulative functional; the theory is descriptive, approximate, and explicitly acknowledged as unlikely to be accurate in detail

conditions: finite framed prospect whose consequences can be represented relative to a neutral reference outcome
either uncertainty represented by state events or the risky special case in which those events carry additive probabilities
task: assign an overall comparative value to a finite prospect from its ordered consequences and associated event information

nodes.description: neutral boundary relative to which consequences are represented as nonnegative or negative changes
finite sequence of possible consequences arranged in increasing outcome order
separation of the ranked consequences into nonnegative and negative branches relative to the neutral boundary
state events associated with the possible consequences; in the risky special case the events carry additive outcome probabilities
two monotone sign-specific set functions evaluated on nested cumulative events, reducing in the risky special case to separate transforms of cumulative probability sums
per-outcome coefficients obtained from differences between successive evaluations of nested cumulative events on the appropriate sign branch
values assigned to consequence changes relative to the neutral boundary, with zero mapped to zero and different curvature permitted above and below the boundary
aggregate value of the nonnegative part obtained by combining its outcome values with its rank-derived coefficients
aggregate value of the negative part obtained by combining its outcome values with its rank-derived coefficients
overall prospect evaluation given by the sum of the nonnegative and negative branch values

relations.description: the neutral boundary determines whether an ordered consequence belongs to the nonnegative or negative branch; it does not itself supply the consequence rank ordering
within each sign branch, outcome rank determines nested cumulative events whose successive sign-specific function values are differenced to obtain the coefficient attached to each outcome
each consequence change relative to the neutral boundary is mapped to an outcome value
outcome values and their rank-derived coefficients are aggregated separately on the nonnegative and negative branches
the overall value of a mixed prospect is the sum of the separately evaluated nonnegative and negative parts
the per-outcome coefficients are not independent transforms of each individual probability; they are marginal contributions derived from sign-specific functions of nested cumulative events
